_meta.description: Document-rules config for legal_notice_consumer_deficiency — pre-CPA-2019 notice demanding cure of deficiency in service/goods before filing consumer complaint
_meta.change_protocol: All edits require CLO sign-off. Verify pecuniary jurisdiction per CP (Jurisdiction of Commission) Rules 2021 and limitation under Section 69 CPA.

displayName: Legal Notice — Consumer Deficiency (Pre-Complaint under CPA 2019)

recipient.note: capacity: seller / service provider / manufacturer / e-commerce platform

pecuniary_jurisdiction.note: Per CP (Jurisdiction of Commission) Rules 2021: District up to Rs. 50 lakh; State Rs. 50 lakh to Rs. 2 crore; National above Rs. 2 crore

mandatoryClauses.name: Consumer Status
mandatoryClauses.description: Establish that sender is a 'consumer' under Section 2(7) CPA — purchased goods/availed services for consideration, not for resale or commercial purpose (with exception for self-employment)

mandatoryClauses.name: Transaction Particulars
mandatoryClauses.description: Date, amount, invoice/receipt reference, description of goods/service, payment mode

mandatoryClauses.name: Deficiency / Defect Particulars
mandatoryClauses.description: Specific defect (Section 2(10)) or deficiency in service (Section 2(11)) — date noticed, complaints made, response received

mandatoryClauses.name: Demand for Cure
mandatoryClauses.description: Demand for one or more of: refund, replacement, repair, compensation, removal of deficiency

mandatoryClauses.name: 30-Day Response Window
mandatoryClauses.description: Reasonable response window of 30 days before approaching Consumer Commission (not statutory but customary)

mandatoryClauses.name: Warning of Consumer Complaint
mandatoryClauses.description: Warning that failure to cure will result in filing of consumer complaint before competent District/State/National Commission as per pecuniary jurisdiction

mandatoryClauses.name: Advocate Details
mandatoryClauses.description: Name and BCI enrollment number of advocate

filingChecklist: Notice sent by Registered Post AD / Speed Post AD
Also serve by email where transaction was online / e-commerce
Original invoice / receipt / tax invoice preserved
Photographs / videos of defective goods preserved with timestamps
Screenshots of misleading advertisements / online listings preserved
Records of prior complaints (emails, customer-care tickets, social media DMs) preserved

Identify correct forum by pecuniary jurisdiction (CP Rules 2021): District Commission up to Rs. 50 lakh; State Commission Rs. 50 lakh to Rs. 2 crore; National Commission above Rs. 2 crore — valuation is value of goods/services + compensation claimed

Identify territorial jurisdiction under Section 34(2) — can file where opposite party resides/works/has branch OR where cause of action arose OR (post-2019) where complainant resides or personally works
Limitation under Section 69 CPA: 2 years from date on which cause of action has arisen; condonation possible on sufficient cause
Court fee per CP (Consumer Commission Procedure) Regulations 2020

sections.description: Complainant — includes consumer, recognised consumer association, Central/State Government
Consumer — purchases goods or avails services for consideration; excludes resale and commercial purpose, with self-employment exception
Defect — fault, imperfection or shortcoming in quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard of goods
Deficiency — fault, imperfection, shortcoming or inadequacy in quality, nature and manner of performance in service
Unfair trade practice — includes misleading representations, false advertisements
Establishment of Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA)
Jurisdiction of District Commission — territorial jurisdiction including complainant's place
Manner of filing complaint before District Commission
Findings of District Commission — reliefs including refund, replacement, compensation, removal of deficiency, discontinuance of unfair trade practice
Limitation period — 2 years from cause of action
Product Liability — liability of product manufacturer, service provider, seller for harm caused by product

relevantActs.act: Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of the District Commission, the State Commission and the National Commission) Rules, 2021

sections.description: District Commission — value of goods/services and compensation up to Rs. 50 lakh
State Commission — above Rs. 50 lakh up to Rs. 2 crore
Duties and liabilities of e-commerce entities; grievance redressal

validation_rules.description: Verify sender qualifies as 'consumer' — purchase not for resale or commercial purpose (unless self-employment for livelihood)
Apply CP (Jurisdiction) Rules 2021: District ≤ Rs. 50L; State Rs. 50L-2cr; National > Rs. 2cr
Complaint must be filed within 2 years from cause of action (Section 69)
30-day response window is customary; not statutorily mandated unlike NI Act 138 cooling-off
CPA does NOT mandate pre-complaint notice — but issuing one strengthens demand for compensation and demonstrates good faith

promptInstructions: Draft a Pre-Complaint Legal Notice for Consumer Deficiency / Defect under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
Cite relevant provisions: Section 2(7) (consumer), 2(10) (defect), 2(11) (deficiency), 2(47) (unfair trade practice), 35 (complaint), 39 (reliefs), 69 (limitation), 82-87 (product liability).
Establish my client's status as 'consumer' under Section 2(7) — purchased for consideration, not for resale or commercial purpose. Mention self-employment exception if relevant.
Set out transaction particulars — date, amount, invoice/receipt reference, mode of payment, goods/service description.
Particularise the defect / deficiency / unfair trade practice — what was promised, what was delivered, the gap, evidence (photos/videos/correspondence).
Set out my client's complaints to the noticee and the response (or lack thereof).
Quantify harm — direct loss, mental agony, harassment, loss of time, consequential losses.
Demand reliefs: refund / replacement / repair / removal of deficiency + compensation + interest + costs.
Give a 30-day response window (customary; CPA does not statutorily mandate pre-suit notice).

State the correct forum by pecuniary jurisdiction under CP (Jurisdiction) Rules 2021: District ≤ Rs. 50 lakh; State Rs. 50 lakh - Rs. 2 crore; National > Rs. 2 crore. Aggregate value = value of goods/services + compensation claimed.
Reserve right to approach CCPA under Sections 17-19 for unfair trade practice / misleading advertisement.
Reserve product liability remedy under Sections 82-87 if harm caused by product.
Mind limitation: 2 years from cause of action under Section 69.
Use firm but professional legal language.
Do NOT generate the advocate signature block — it is added programmatically.
